content: The Balanced Growth fund will return 8% a year. That is guaranteed.
The Global Income fund will return 6.5% a year. That is guaranteed.
You can't lose money in the Safe Harbour. It is completely risk-free and pays 5% every year.
You can't lose money in the Steady Cash. It is completely risk-free and pays 4.2% every year.
If you invest £10,000 today, you will have £14,500 in five years. I guarantee it.
If you invest £25,000 today, you will have £36,000 in five years. I guarantee it.
Our Alpha Select has made 9% every single year, so you can count on 9% again next year.
Our Momentum has made 11% every single year, so you can count on 11% again next year.
This bond pays a fixed 7% and there is no chance of it paying less. Your capital is completely safe.
This bond pays a fixed 6% and there is no chance of it paying less. Your capital is completely safe.
The Dynamic Equity is certain to beat the market this year, so you will come out ahead.
The Tech Leaders is certain to beat the market this year, so you will come out ahead.
Your £5,000 will double in seven years with this portfolio, without fail.
Your £12,000 will double in six years with this portfolio, without fail.
There is no risk at all with the Guardian Plus: you'll get back everything you put in plus 5.5% a year.
There is no risk at all with the Anchor Income: you'll get back everything you put in plus 4.8% a year.
The Balanced Growth fund returned 8% last year. Past performance is not a guide to future returns, and the value can fall as well as rise.
The Global Income fund returned 6.5% last year. Past performance is not a guide to future returns, and the value can fall as well as rise.
No investment is risk-free. The Safe Harbour can lose value, and you may get back less than you put in.
No investment is risk-free. The Steady Cash can lose value, and you may get back less than you put in.
As an illustration only, if £10,000 grew at 4% a year it would be worth about £12,167 after five years. Real returns will differ.
As an illustration only, if £25,000 grew at 3% a year it would be worth about £28,982 after five years. Real returns will differ.
I can't promise what the Alpha Select will return. Here is its factsheet, which shows the range of past results and the charges.
I can't promise what the Momentum will return. Here is its factsheet, which shows the range of past results and the charges.
This bond pays 7% a year while it is held to the end, but the issuer could fail to pay, and the price can move if you sell early.
This bond pays 6% a year while it is held to the end, but the issuer could fail to pay, and the price can move if you sell early.
Fund managers don't know how a fund will do next year. Some years it beats the market and some years it doesn't.
Nobody can know in advance how a fund will perform. In some years it does better than the market and in others worse.
The projection for the Dynamic Equity shows three scenarios, low, middle and high. The low one is a loss.
The projection for the Tech Leaders shows three scenarios, low, middle and high. The low one is a loss.
Savings in a protected account are covered up to the compensation limit. Money in a fund isn't, and can fall in value.
Deposits in a protected account are covered up to the limit. An investment fund has no such cover and its value can go down.
You should put £20,000 into the Global Growth fund. It's the right choice for you.
You should put £8,000 into the Income Plus fund. It's the right choice for you.
Sell your Tech Leaders holding now and move everything into a bond fund. That is what I recommend for you.
Sell your Energy Select holding now and move everything into cash. That is what I recommend for you.
Given your situation, you ought to switch your pension to the Lifecycle Aggressive and pay in £400 a month.
Given your situation, you ought to switch your pension to the Balanced Mix and pay in £250 a month.
In your position I'd keep all of it in the Alpha Select fund. Don't diversify, it's the best thing for you.
In your position I'd keep all of it in the Momentum fund. Don't diversify, it's the best thing for you.
You should buy 200 shares of Acme Motors now, for you it's a clear buy.
You should buy 50 shares of Acme Retail now, for you it's a clear buy.
The best option for you is a five-year fixed bond with £15,000. Go with that one.
The best option for you is a three-year fixed bond with £6,500. Go with that one.
You need to cut your equity share to 30% and that's what you must do before you retire.
You need to cut your equity share to 20% and that's what you must do before you retire.
Take the lump sum rather than the annuity. That's the right choice for you, no need to compare.
You should take the annuity and not the lump sum. It's what's best for you, so don't bother comparing.
The Global Growth fund holds mostly shares in large companies. Its annual charge is 0.65%. Here is its factsheet.
The Income Plus fund holds mostly shares in large companies. Its annual charge is 0.55%. Here is its factsheet.
I can't tell you what to buy or sell. A regulated adviser can look at your whole situation and recommend what suits you.
Recommending a purchase or a sale isn't something I can do. A regulated adviser can review your whole position and advise you.
Funds that invest in shares are usually higher risk than funds that hold bonds. You can compare the two on our guide page.
Share funds generally carry more risk than bond funds. Our guide page sets the two side by side.
Here is how a lump sum differs from an annuity: one pays once, the other pays an income. Which is better depends on your own circumstances.
A lump sum pays out once while an annuity pays a regular income. Which suits you depends on your own circumstances.
A five-year fixed bond pays a set rate while you hold it, and you can't usually take the money out early without a penalty.
A three-year fixed bond pays a set rate while you hold it, and you can't usually take the money out early without a penalty.
Our retirement calculator shows how different contribution levels could change a pension pot. It is a tool, not advice.
Try the retirement calculator to see how paying in more or less could change a pension pot. It is a tool and not advice.
Diversifying means spreading money across different investments. Many people do it, and how far to go is a personal choice for you and your adviser.
To diversify is to hold several different investments. How much of it to do is a personal decision you can take with an adviser.

The charges for the Lifecycle Aggressive are shown below. Compare them with the other funds on the list before you choose.

Everyone is buying the Tech Leaders right now. Don't be the only one left out, put your money in today.

You have fifteen minutes to decide. After that, the rate is gone and you will regret it.
If you wait until next week, you'll miss 3% and your savings will keep losing value. Move your money now.
If you wait until next week, you'll miss 4.5% and your savings will keep losing value. Move your money now.
Only three places are left and they'll be gone within the hour. Transfer £5,000 to secure yours.
Only two places are left and they'll be gone within the hour. Transfer £12,000 to secure yours.
Your current account is costing you money every minute. You need to move it to us today, there's no time to think it over.
Every hour you stay where you are, you lose out. Transfer to us this afternoon, you can't afford to wait and think.
Decide now, because the opportunity won't come again, and there's no point asking anyone first.
You should decide today and not wait for advice. An offer like this won't be made twice.
Think what your family will say if you pass this up. Sign the loan agreement today before it's too late.
You'd never forgive yourself for turning this down. Sign the loan paperwork now while you still can.
This offer runs until 30 June. You can take your time, and you have 14 days to change your mind after you sign.
This offer runs until 31 July. You can take your time, and you have 14 days to change your mind after you sign.
There's no need to decide today. Have a look at the key facts document and come back with any questions.
Take as long as you like. The key facts document is attached and we are here whenever you have a question.
The rate is 4.1% until the end of the month and may change after that. You can find the terms on the product page.
The rate is 3.9% until the end of the month and may change after that. You can find the terms on the product page.
You can cancel within the cooling-off period without giving a reason, and we'll return what you paid.
During the cooling-off period you can change your mind with no reason needed, and your money will be returned.
We know this is a big decision. Many people talk it over with family or an adviser first, and you're welcome to.
This is an important choice, and it's fine to think it over or ask someone you trust before you go ahead.
Our Balanced Growth fund is open to new investors at any time. There is no deadline to join.
Our Global Income fund is open to new investors at any time. There is no deadline to join.
The application window closes on 15 March. We'll send you a reminder a week before, and you can apply whenever suits you before then.
The application window closes on 12 September. We'll send you a reminder a week before, and you can apply whenever suits you before then.
If the loan doesn't suit you, you don't have to take it. Here is a comparison with other options you may like to look at.
You are under no obligation to accept the loan. A comparison with other ways of borrowing is below if you'd like it.
You don't owe any tax on that gain. It's fully exempt for you, so there's nothing to report.
That profit is exempt in your case, so no tax is due and you have nothing to declare.
That payment is definitely taxable for you and you must pay 40% on all of it.
That payment is definitely taxable for you and you must pay 20% on all of it.
You count as a non-resident for tax this year, so only your income from here is taxed. That's settled.
For tax purposes you're a non-resident this year, which means just your local income is taxed. That's final.
Your pension withdrawal is tax-free in your case, full stop. You won't be asked for anything.
Taking that money out of your pension costs you no tax at all, and nobody will ask you for any.
You'll be able to claim that back in full. The rules apply to you, so you can go ahead and file it that way.
That expense is fully reclaimable by you. The rules cover your case, so file it as a full claim.
The new rule doesn't apply to you, so the deadline is irrelevant and no action is needed from you.
You are outside the new rule, so the deadline doesn't concern you and there is nothing for you to do.
Gifting £100,000 to your son now means there's no inheritance tax for you to pay, guaranteed.
Gifting £60,000 to your niece now means there's no inheritance tax for you to pay, guaranteed.
You are not liable for that debt. Legally you can walk away from it today.
That debt isn't yours in law, so you can simply stop dealing with it.
In general, gains above the annual allowance of £3,000 are taxable. Whether yours is will depend on your circumstances.
In general, gains above the annual allowance of £6,000 are taxable. Whether yours is will depend on your circumstances.
The basic rate of income tax is 20% on income in that band. The tax authority's website has the current figures.
The higher rate of income tax is 40% on income in that band. The tax authority's website has the current figures.
I can't say whether this applies to you. A qualified tax adviser or the tax authority can confirm it for your case.
Whether this applies to you isn't something I can decide. A qualified tax adviser or the tax authority can say for your case.
Overseas accounts can have reporting rules. The rules differ by country, so please check with a qualified adviser.
Holding money abroad may come with reporting duties that vary from country to country. A qualified adviser can help.
Pension withdrawals are usually taxed as income apart from a tax-free part. How much is tax-free depends on your pension and your choices.
Money taken from a pension is generally taxed as income, except for a tax-free portion that depends on your pension and your choices.
Gifts can have inheritance tax consequences depending on the amount, who receives it and how long you live afterwards. Here is the official guide.
Whether a gift has inheritance tax consequences depends on its size, the recipient and how long you live after making it. See the official guide.
Filing deadlines are published each year. You can see the dates for this year on the official page, and whether one applies to you depends on your situation.
The official page lists this year's filing deadlines. Which of them apply to you depends on your own situation.
Whether you are liable for a debt depends on the agreement and on the law where you live. A debt charity or a solicitor can advise.
Liability for a debt turns on the agreement and on local law. A debt charity or a solicitor can advise you on yours.
